FTA with Thailand
†*141. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI JANARDAN
DWIVEDI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the terms of Free Trade Agreement
with Thailand;
(b) whether it is also a fact that due to
heavy reduction in the import duty on 82
items imported from Thailand, the goods
of Thailand are cheaper than that of India;
(c) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to save Indian industry from
closure; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Producing energy from garbage
*142. SHRI R. SHUNMUGA-
SUNDARAM: Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) the subsidy given for power projects
using garbage as raw material;
(b) the other similar projects which get
subsidy;
(c) the number of units which produce
energy from garbage commissioned so far
and the quantum of electricity produced;
and
(d) the number of more such units likely
to be established this year?
Declaration of NIFT as deemed
university
*143. SHRI LALITBHAI MEHTA:
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the National Institute of
Fashion Technology awards any degree to
those who complete four years' study
successfully;
(b) to which university, the above
Institute is affiliated;
(c) if the Institute is not affiliated to
any university, what is its academic status
in awarding degrees and make the degree
holders employable;
(d) whether Government intend to
declare NIFT as a deemed university, if so,
by when the decision would be taken;
and

44
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(e) whether the students admitted in
NIFT, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, have any
residential facility by way of hostels owned
by the Ministry of Textiles?
Floods in Madhya Pradesh
†*144. SHRI P. K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken by Government to
provide assistance to the farmers affected
by devastating floods in Madhya Pradesh;
(b) the extent of loss to agriculture in
the State by the floods this year; and
(c) whether Government have provided
in full the relief assistance demanded by
the State Government for facing this
calamity?
Sale of properties of NTC
*145. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had invited bids for the sale of properties
of the National Textiles Corporation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government had received bid for the sale
of property of Mumbai Textile Mill of
NTC; and
(d) whether Government are considering
to use the proceeds of sale of properties of
NTC for the revival of other sick NTC
Mills?
Supreme Court verdict on IMDT Act
*146. SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court of India
has struck down the Illegal Migrants
(Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983 as
unconstitutional, holding it responsible for
delaying detection and deportation of
foreigners in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Annual turnover in retail market
†*147. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether any assessment has been
made by Government regarding annual
turnover in retail market in country;
(b) if so, the value of annual turnover in
the retail market;
(c) the estimates of the value of the
business of this market increased on an
average during the last three years; and
(d) the status of Indian retail market in
comparison with business in retail markets
of other countries in the world?
"Bharat Nirman" scheme
*148. SHRI R. P. GOENKA: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently a
detailed programme for the renewal of rural
infrastructure, with a massive initial
investment of Rs. 1,74,000 crores, under
the composite "Bharat Nirman" scheme
has been formulated; and
(b) if so, the details thereof, including
the critical areas of rural infrastructure
identified for special focus, the time-frame
fixed for implementation and the sources
of funding decided upon?

45
Steps to retain pilots of Armed Forces
*149. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of pilots of Armed Forces
who had quit the service during the last
three years, showing the force each had
served togetherwith the length of service;
(b) whether it is a fact that more and
more pilots are leaving the forces for greener
pastures with the MNCs 'outside'; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
check this trend?
Reduction of troops on J & K border
†*150. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the number of soldiers have
been reduced on the border of Jammu and
Kashmir;
(b) whether there is a decline in the cross-
border terrorist activities being carried out
by Pakistan; and
(c) whether Pakistan have also reduced
the number of soldiers on its border and
accepted the Indian Line of Control and if
so, the details thereof ?
Violence against women
†*151. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
officials or police personnel too commit
violence against women in the country;
(b) if so, whether Government propose
to enact stringent laws and amend the
present Criminal Procedure Code; and
(c) if so, by when and the reasons for
the delay therein?
Installation of power plants in the
country
†*152. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA:
PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering to install power plants in
the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the amount likely to be spent by
Government on the installation of the power
plants?
Framing of long-term policy on
exports of raw materials used for
making steel
*153. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are in the
process of framing long-term policy on
exports of raw materials used to make steel;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the production of iron ore in
the country during the last five years,
year-wise?
Cultivable land with irrigation
facilities
*154. SHRI JANARDAN
DWIVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

46
(a) the area of cultivable land with
assured irrigation facilities in the beginning
of the Ninth and Tenth Five Year Plans and
the area of such land without such facilities;
and
(b) the area of such land brought under
irrigation facilities during 2004-05; each year
of the Tenth Plan earlier and the expenditure
incurred in regard to and the growth rate
registered year to year in this regard?
Export of clothes
†*155. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH: Will the Minister of TEXTILES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to increase the target of export of clothes
during the year 2005-06; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Fall in industrial production
*156. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Index for industrial
production fell to 4.9 per cent during
February, 2005 compared to 8.3 per cent
registered in February, 2004;
(b) if so, the main reasons for the
negative growth in 2005 and the steps
Government propose to take to improve
the industrial growth during 2005-06;
and
(c) to what extent these steps have been
able to improve the industrial growth in
the country?
Floods in the country
*157. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether floods have caused havoc
in many States of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
amount of loss caused to each State;
(c) whether Government have provided
relief and given grants to overcome the
situation; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken to check floods?
Law to protect witnesses
*158. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in the absence
of a law to protect the rights of victims/
witnesses, in many cases, crucial witnesses
turn hostile, making the present laws
useless;
(b) whether any committee has
recommended enactment of a law giving
protection to the witnesses;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether Government have any
proposal to bring forth a Bill to protect
witnesses' rights?
Appointment of special envoy to deal
with naxal violence
*159. SHRI S. M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have evolved a proposal to appoint a
Special Envoy to deal with different States
on naxalite violence;

NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 28th July, 2005 Secretary-General.
Sravana  6, 1927 (Saka)
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
this Special Envoy will try to bring diverse
factions involved in naxalite violence to the
conference table;
(c) the details of the role of Government
in evolving a nation-wide formula for talks
with various naxalite outfits;
(d) whether it is a fact that Government
had also discussed this matter
with the Andhra Pradesh Government;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
FTA among Asian countries
*160. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any possibility of
Free Trade Agreement materialising among
Asian countries; if so, the details thereof;
and
(b) what is likely to be the impact of
this agreement on the automobile industry
in the country?

Foreign capital investment in retail
market
†954. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a demand
has been made in a study report issued by
certain private sector institutions that
foreign capital investment may be increased
by 49 per cent in retail market;
(b) if so, the names of such institutions
and the details of the study reports
forwarded by these institutions to
Government during last three years;
(c) whether Government have made any
cost benefit analysis on this report on retail
market; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Industrial sickness
955. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the current level of industrial sickness
in the country;
(b) the steps being taken/proposed to
be taken to find out the reasons for
industrial sickness and for their revival in a
time bound manner;
(c) the number of references made to
BIFR during each of the last three years
and the number of industries recommended
for revival by BIFR, State-wise; and
(d) the number of such sick industries
revived during each of the last three years,
State-wise?
Target Plus Scheme
956. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a fresh
notification has been issued to accord the
benefits of the Target Plus Scheme by now
by the Directorate of Foreign Trade;
(b) if so, how many applications for
this scheme have been received by DGFT
for the period from 8th to 20th April, 2005;
and
(c) what are the reasons and who are
responsible for keeping this scheme in
abeyance  after announcing it since
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

218
8th April, 2005 till the issue of fresh
notification?
Impact of sanitary and phytosanitary
standards on farm-exports
957. SHRI R.K. ANAND:
SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether country's farm-export is
facing non-tariff barriers due to sanitary
and phytosanitary standards by some
countries;
(b) if so, how many such cases been
reported in the past three years and what
steps have been taken;
(c) whether these sanitary and
phytosanitary standards are in line with
WTO agreements, if so, the details of such
provisions and do we comply with such
standards; and
(d) what steps are being taken to
safeguard country's farm-exports from such
non-tariff barriers?
Bilateral trade with BIMST countries
958. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that while our
bilateral trade with other countries is
picking up, the Bangladesh, India,
Myanmar, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka and
Thailand Economic Cooperation (BIMST)
Treaty has not resulted in any appreciable
economic cooperation;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) what is the action plan of
Government to smoothen the process to
facilitate an upswing in the bilateral trade
with these countries as well?
Videsh Krishi Upaj Yojana
959. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) what are the salient features of
Videsh Krishi Upaj Yojana;
(b) since when this is being
implemented; and
(c) the details of achievements of this
scheme so far?
MFN status in Indo-Pak trade
960. SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS KAUR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether during the recent visit of
Pak President to New Delhi he pointed out
that the tariff barriers in India were not in
tandem with the Most Favoured Nation
status granted by India in respect of Pak-
goods;
(b) whether it is a fact that most of the
to-and-fro trade with Pakistan is made
through Dubai; if so, the extent of the two
way trade done with Pakistan through
Dubai and other channels during 2004-05
and 2005-06 so far; and
(c) the steps since taken to translate the
MFN status in Indo-Pak trade in absolute
terms?
Functions of APEDA
961. SHRI S.S. CHANDRAN: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the major functions of Agricultural

219
and Processed Food Products Export
Development Authority (APEDA);
(b) its location and branches, if any;
and
(c) its  contribution in promoting
exports?
Fall in seafood exports after Tsunami
962. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether seafood export and number
of seafood exporters especially shrimp
exports fell sharply after Tsunami of
December 2004;
(b) if so, the details including number of
exporters associated with shrimp export
to US, quantity of shrimp exported to
United States and the amount of foreign
exchange received during the period January
2004 to June 2005, month-wise and
category-wise;
(c) the details of action taken to protect
sea export especially shrimp export;
(d) whether any action is being taken to
revoke anti-dumping duties imposed on
shrimp from India by US;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
New subjects in protocol of WTO
963. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
WTO is including new subjects and new
areas without proper approval from
Member-countries like India;
(b) whether it is a fact that the WTO
has included new subjects like
'Competition Policy', Labour standards,
etc., which were not in the original
protocols of WTO;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government has not lodged any formal
protest with WTO;
(d) if so, the reasons for Government
not raising this issue in the proper fora;
and
(e) the steps proposed in this regard by
Government?
Proposal to counter trade barriers in
WTO talks
964. SHRIMATI N. P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) how the Government propose to
dispute the non-tariff barriers and the
phytosanitary barriers imposed by certain
developed countries in the coming WTO
talks;
(b) whether any consultations have
been held with experts in this field;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) what are the other areas that are
going to come up for discussion in WTO
talks at Hong Kong?
Rejection of export consignments
965. DR. VIJAY MALLYA:
SHRI EKANATH K.
THAKUR:
SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that large
consignments mainly of food items were
rejected by the authorities in US, EU, UK,
Poland, etc. in the month of May this
year;

220
(b) if so, what were the reasons for such
heavy rejection; and
(c) what action is proposed to be taken
to ensure that export consignments are not
rejected by the consignee Governments?
Revival of sick industrial units
†966. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE

March, 2004 to June, 2005 Government
have made several announcements for
providing financial relief to sick industrial
units;
(b) if so, the dates of the announcements
made and the amount provided under each
announcement; and
(c) the names of institutions which were
given relief and the amount provided to
each of them till July, 2005?

Minister of COMMERCE AND

(a) whether it is a fact that  our seafood
exports have gone up considerably in spite
of anti-dumping duty imposed by certain
countries;
(b) if so, the amount of exports during
2004-05 and the share of Orissa State out
of this lot;
(c) which are our major markets; and
(d) the action plan of Government to
persuade those countries which are
continuing with levy of anti-dumping
duties on our exports to withdraw these
duties?
FDI in SEZ
968. SHRIMATI  HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have been able to make a strong pitch for
forcing investment in India at the World
Economic Forum in the recent past in
Davos, Switzerland;
(b) whether any policy measures taken
to attract FDI in the Special Economic Zone
(SEZ); and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Import of fruits
969. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of fruits imported after
the removal of import restrictions showing
the quantum of each fruit variety;
(b) the customs duty imposed on each
of these imported fruit varieties; and
(c) how far it has affected the domestic
fruit growers/traders?
Industrial development centres

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the number of industrial
development centres opened in the country
including the number of such centres
opened in Uttar Pradesh during the year
2004-05;
(b) the amount of funds provided by
Government for industrial development
centres in Uttar Pradesh during last three
years; and

(c) the number of such  centres  likely
to be opened in future?
Effect of FTAs and PTAs on spices

INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

Preferential Trade Agreements between
India and neighbouring countries spices that
are not grown and are more than production
levels are landing in Indian market as
produce of those nations;
(b) if so, the details of quantity of
pepper, cardamom (small), clove, star anise
and valuation of these spices imported
under Open General Licence arrived in
Indian  ports from Nepal, Pakistan, Sri
Lanka and Bangladesh between April, 2003
and July, 2005, category-wise and country-
wise species;
(c) the action taken to protect domestic
market for spices, and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Export and import by State Trading
Corporation
†972. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that State Trading
Corporation is carrying out exports and
imports;
(b) the value of the export and import
carried out during 2003-04, 2004-05 and
first quarter of 2005-06;
(c) the percentage, above value
constitutes of the total values of export
and import carried out from country during
each of the above period; and
(d) the role of above organization in
foreign trade after adoption of liberalization
policy in respect of export and import prior
to a decade?
Terminal at Wagha border to facilitate
trade
†973. SHRI R.S. GAVAI: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India is setting
up a terminal at Wagha border in order to
facilitate trade with Pakistan;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) in what way India will benefit by
this terminal?
Issues to be raised by India in WTO
conference at Hong Kong

SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) what are the preparations made by
Government and what are the issues on
which India is going to emphasise in the
forthcoming Ministerial Conference of
WTO at Hong Kong;
(b) whether there is a possibility of
taking up these issues, apart from
agriculture in the Ministerial meeting;
(c) if so, what are the possible issues

(d) whether any consultations have
been held with experts in connection with
agriculture related aspects which are going
to be placed before the Ministerial meeting;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?

Strategy for WTO meeting at
Hong Kong
975. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND

its strategy for the WTO Ministerial level
talks scheduled to take place in Hong Kong,

tariff reduction, reduction in subsidies in
developing countries, trade distorting
domestic support by developed countries
in the agricultural sector, TRIPS on account
of public health, etc.;
(b) if so, whether a consensus is also
being tried to be evolved in such vital
matters with leading political parties; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Indo-Japan bilateral trade
976. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as a result of
the recent visit of the Prime Minister of

companies operating in India in 2005 and

(c) what is the action plan of both the
countries to further strengthen their
economic relations to contribute more to
the development and prosperity of India?
International Trade Fairs in various
parts of the country

the Minister of COMMERCE AND

proposal to organize International Trade
Fairs in various parts of the country to
promote country's trade with other
countries; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE

(a) whether Government propose to set
up 1500 crores industrial estates in East
India;
(b) if so, what is the share of investment
for North East Region industrial estates
with particular reference to Assam;
(c) by when such industrial estates are
likely to be set up in the North East Region;
(d) the details thereof indicating the
projects likely to come up; and
(e) whether industrial estates already
existing in the North East Region, which
are in bad condition, are likely to be
revitalised; if so, the details thereof and if
not, the reasons therefor?
Steps to promote consumption of
coffee in Karnataka
979. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state the various
steps taken to promote domestic
consumption of coffee in Karnataka?
Steps to improve trade with Japan

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India's trade

223
with Japan slided in last decade of post
reform era from third largest trading partner
to seventh largest;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) what are the items and their value
exported to and imported from Japan during
last three years; and
(d) the steps being taken to improve
bilateral trade with Japan?
Steps to boost agricultural exports

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the total
agricultural exports from India grew by only
3.9 per cent in 2004-05;
(b) whether it is a fact that the export of
marine products (the largest exported
commodity) from India fell by 6.7 per cent
